changes: Three exercises a day instead of four: warm-up, ear game, then one longer piece that turns the day's idea into music, so the day reads as one lesson.
The why gives the student a check they can use alone ("smooth means in tune, a wobble means off"), not only what it improves.
The ear games ask the student to hum or sing the notes back before answering, linking the ear to the voice.
Every day's last block is the student's own: a tune from Do Re Mi, their own skips, their own line over chords.
The long Do is compared by feel ("how much steadier than day 1"), not by counting clicks on day 1 and day 7.

note: The voice-beginner week in the new teaching style: same keys, tunes and tools, but three exercises a day (warm-up, ear game, one longer musical piece), each why gives the student a way to check themselves, and every day ends with something they make up.

plan.title: Week 1: Do Mi Sol, in tune, your way
plan.summary: Sing in tune over a drone and skip through Do Mi Sol, one idea a day: each day a short warm-up, an ear game, and a longer musical piece that ends with a tune or line you make up.

exercises.title: Find the smooth spot
exercises.focus: Do over a C drone
exercises.why: In tune with the drone sounds smooth and off sounds like a wobble, so the drone lets you check yourself with no one listening.

sections.text: Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff as a line. Sing {{1}} on "oo" and slide a little above and below it until the wobble stops. Hold the smooth spot for as long as feels easy.

exercises.title: Steps or skips?
exercises.focus: Hear a step (Do-Re) from a skip (Do-Mi, jumping over Re)
exercises.why: Melodies move by steps and skips, so hearing which is which tells you where the next note is before you sing it.

sections.text: Press Start below. The game plays two notes, a step or a skip: hum the two back, then answer.

exercises.title: Step tunes, then your own
exercises.focus: Two easy step tunes in C · a tune of your own on Do Re Mi
exercises.why: Step tunes use notes right next to each other, so they train your voice to move one note at a time and stay in tune.

sections.text: A step tune
Press Play on the tune to hear it, then start the mic and sing it on the note names: they help you remember each sound.
Another one
The same kind of tune, a new shape. Sing it on "la" once you know it.
Your own

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff as a line. Make up a short tune from {{1}}, {{2}} and {{3}} on "la", ending on {{1}}. Make another that starts on {{3}}.

exercises.title: Hum, then open
exercises.focus: Do and Sol over a D drone
exercises.why: Humming keeps the sound small and easy to tune, so opening to "ah" from a hum carries the in-tune note with it.

sections.text: Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff as a line. Hum {{1}} with your lips closed, then open to "ah" and skip up to {{5}}. Listen for the smooth spot on both.

exercises.title: 3rd or 5th?
exercises.focus: Hear Do-Mi from Do-Sol
exercises.why: Mi and Sol are the two notes a skip from Do usually lands on, so telling them apart is half of singing a skip in tune.

sections.text: Press Start below. The game plays Do and then Mi or Sol: sing the second note back on "la", then answer.

exercises.title: A skipping tune, then over chords
exercises.focus: An easy skipping tune in D · Do and Sol over D and A
exercises.why: A skip lands on a chord note, so a tune that skips is really the chord sung one note at a time.

sections.text: A skipping tune
Press Play on the tune to hear it, then start the mic and sing it on the note names.
Over the chords
Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the chords. On "ah", sing {{1}} when D comes round and {{5}} when A does. Then try {{3}} over D and hear how it changes the colour.

exercises.title: A long Do in G
exercises.focus: Do over a G drone, held
exercises.why: A long note shows every wobble in your pitch line, so holding Do steady trains the breath that keeps every note in tune.

sections.text: Press Start exercise below: the drone, the metronome and the mic start together. Sing {{1}} on "oo" and hold it while your line stays flat. Breathe when you need to and go again.

exercises.title: 5th or 6th?
exercises.focus: Hear Do-Sol from Do-La
exercises.why: La sits one step above Sol, so hearing the two apart is what lets you sing the step between them.

sections.text: Press Start below. The game plays Do and then Sol or La: hum the second note, then answer.

exercises.title: Sol La Sol, then over chords
exercises.focus: An easy tune on Sol and La in G · over G and D
exercises.why: La is the step above Sol that tunes lean on and fall back from, so a tune on the two is the first move away from the chord.

sections.text: Sol La Sol
Press Play on the tune to hear it, then start the mic and sing it on the note names.
Over G and D
Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the chords. On "ah", make up a line from the low {{1}}, {{3}} and {{5}} that changes when the chord does.

exercises.title: Siren to Sol
exercises.focus: Slide from Do to Sol over an F drone
exercises.why: A slow slide passes through every pitch on the way, so it shows your voice the whole distance it needs to skip.

sections.text: Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff as a line. On "oo", slide slowly from the low {{1}} up to {{5}} and back, like a siren, then sing the two as a clean skip.

exercises.title: Skips, falling
exercises.focus: Hear a falling 3rd from a falling 5th
exercises.why: Tunes fall as often as they rise, and a falling skip feels different, so hear it the way down too.

sections.text: Press Start below. The game plays a note and then a lower one, a 3rd or a 5th below: hum the lower note back, then answer.

exercises.title: A tune under Do, then over three chords
exercises.focus: An easy tune that dips under Do in F · over F, B♭ and C
exercises.why: Tunes often dip below Do and come home, so singing under it makes Do feel like home from both sides.

sections.text: A tune under Do
Press Play on the tune to hear it, then start the mic and sing it on the note names.
Over F, B♭ and C
Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the chords. On "ah", sing the low {{4}} when B♭ comes round and find your own way back to {{1}}.

days.theme: Do Mi Sol in a new key

exercises.title: Do Mi Sol in A
exercises.focus: Do Mi Sol over an A drone
exercises.why: Do Mi Sol sounds the same in every key, so moving it to A shows your ear knows the shape, not the notes.

sections.text: Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff as a line. Sing {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} up and back on the note names, then skip straight from {{1}} to {{5}}.

exercises.title: Steps and skips, mixed
exercises.focus: Hear steps, 3rds and 5ths
exercises.why: Real tunes mix steps and skips, so hearing them mixed is closer to singing a song than hearing them alone.

sections.text: Press Start below. The game plays a step, a 3rd or a 5th: hum it back, then answer.

exercises.title: A harder skipping tune, then your own
exercises.focus: A medium skipping tune in A · your own skips
exercises.why: A harder tune puts the skips closer together, and then making up your own shows which skips you hear best.

sections.text: A harder skipping tune
Press Play on the tune to hear it, then start the mic and sing it on "la".
Your own skips
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff as a line. Make up a tune of skips between {{1}}, {{3}} and {{5}} on "la", ending on {{1}}.

exercises.title: Do Re Mi Re Do
exercises.focus: Do Re Mi and back over a C drone
exercises.why: A step up and back is the shape most tunes start with, so it trains the exact move songs ask for.

sections.text: Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff as a line. Sing {{1}} {{2}} {{3}} {{2}} {{1}} on the note names, then on "oo".

exercises.title: Hear and sing back
exercises.focus: Sing back a 3rd or a 5th
exercises.why: Singing back what you hear links your ear to your voice, which is what learning a tune by ear is.

sections.text: Press Start below. The game plays a 3rd or a 5th: sing both notes back on "la" before you answer.

exercises.title: Steps, then 3rds
exercises.focus: A medium step tune · an easy tune in 3rds, in C
exercises.why: Steps and 3rds are the two moves most tunes use, so a tune of each is the week in two songs.

sections.text: A step tune
Press Play on the tune to hear it, then start the mic and sing it on the note names.
A tune in 3rds
Press Play on the tune to hear it, then start the mic and sing it on "la". Notice where it steps and where it skips.

exercises.title: A long Do, then and now
exercises.focus: Do over a D drone, held
exercises.why: Holding Do steady is where the week started, so it is the clearest place to feel how far you've come.

sections.text: Press Start exercise below: the drone, the metronome and the mic start together. Sing {{1}} on "ah" and hold it. Notice how much steadier your line is than on day 1.

exercises.title: The week's intervals
exercises.focus: Steps, 3rds, 5ths and 6ths
exercises.why: Every interval from this week in one game shows which ones your ear now knows by itself.

sections.text: Press Start below. The game plays any interval from this week: sing it back, then answer.

exercises.title: A Sol tune, then your own line
exercises.focus: An easy Sol tune in D · your own line over D, G and A
exercises.why: You have sung Do, Mi, Sol and La over chords this week, so now you can choose them yourself.

sections.text: A Sol tune
Press Play on the tune to hear it, then start the mic and sing it on the note names.
Your own line
Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the chords. Make up your own line from {{1}}, {{3}} and {{5}} on "ah", one that moves when the chords do and ends on {{1}}.
